Acquisition Agreement Clause:
Section 9.12. Evaluation of Acquisition Offers. (a) Notwithstanding any prior provisions, upon receipt of any written acquisition offer not arising out of a breach of this Agreement, the Board is required to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the offer. In so doing, the Board shall: (i) evaluate the financial metrics of the offer; (ii) assess strategic and operational synergies as detailed in the supplementary Memorandum appended hereto; (iii) engage in good faith consultations with external legal counsel and industry advisors; and (iv) deliberate on potential impacts on shareholder value, including but not limited to non-financial risks and long-term governance implications. (b) An offer shall be designated a Superior Proposal only if post-negotiation, the Board determines that the complete spectrum of financial, strategic, and fiduciary criteria justify such designation. (c) In circumstances where the financial aspects are particularly prominent, the Board is nevertheless mandated to ensure that such prominence does not obscure other material non-financial considerations outlined herein.

(a) The Board shall, in its initial assessment, subject each Acquisition Proposal to a rigorous financial analysis, including but not limited to revenue projections, cost synergies, and market valuation, to determine if the proposal meets the baseline financial threshold.
(b) Notwithstanding clause (a), before a proposal is finally designated as a Superior Proposal, the Board is required to:
   (i) Consult with its independent legal and regulatory advisors to ensure compliance with all applicable statutory and fiduciary obligations;
   (ii) Engage in a series of stakeholder negotiations to consider the qualitative merits of the proposal, including strategic fit and associated risk assessments;
   (iii) Reevaluate the initial financial analysis in light of any modifications resulting from the consultations and negotiations.
(c) Even if the financial metrics substantially exceed the baseline threshold, clauses (b)(i) and (b)(ii) remain mandatory and must be fully complied with.
(d) For purposes of this Section, a Superior Proposal is defined as one that, after full compliance with clauses (a) through (c), demonstrates a net advantage across both financial and non-financial parameters.
